entities.name: ChIP-seq cofactor motif enrichment
observations: ENCODE analysis of 425 experiments, 122 TFs, and approximately 1.7 million peaks found TF- and cell-type-specific enrichment of non-target cofactor motifs, including predicted interactions.

entities.name: ENCODE CAP motif co-enrichment
observations: In HepG2 occupancy maps covering 208 chromatin-associated proteins, motifs for other TFs were frequently co-enriched; FOX-family motifs occurred in peaks of 37 other proteins.
High-occupancy regions can contain many associated proteins while motifs explain only a subset, consistent with indirect recruitment or chromatin-state effects.

entities.name: ChIP-seq motif quality signal
observations: Analysis of 427 human TF ChIP-seq datasets recovered target-factor specificity while identifying potential cofactor motifs; motif patterns informed cooperativity, cell-type specificity, antibody specificity, and problematic-dataset assessment.

entities.name: Indirect TF occupancy
observations: Non-target motif enrichment can reflect cooperative recruitment, tethering, indirect DNA binding, or shared enhancer/promoter chromatin environments; a ChIP peak does not prove direct binding by every motif-associated TF.

entities.name: ChIP-seq motif artifacts
observations: Some apparent non-target motif enrichment can arise from antibody cross-reactivity, nonspecific immunoprecipitation, high-occupancy regions, GC or sequence-composition bias, peak-calling choices, and inadequate controls.

entities.name: Accessibility-conditioned motif grammar
observations: Motif co-enrichment is conditioned by accessible enhancer/promoter chromatin and cell state; spacing, orientation, and positional relationships can help distinguish functional partnerships from generic sequence overlap.
